newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: ALPINE SKIING-TOMBA SEIZES FIRST VICTORY OF SEASON.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-TOMBA SEIZES FIRST VICTORY OF SEASON.

text.p: Italian Alberto Tomba seized his first victory of the season in a men's World Cup night slalom on Thursday, proving his fitness for his home Alpine skiing world championships in Sestriere.
Tomba clocked an aggregate time of one minute 35.87 seconds on the Planai piste, and is now anxious for the February 16 championship slalom which will also be raced under floodlights.
"It was very important for me to win a race before Sestriere," said Tomba. "This gives me confidence. Now I have two weeks to continue preparing for Sestriere."
Austria's first-run leader Thomas Stangassinger was second (1:36.03) despite a mistake in the middle section, while Frenchman Sebastien Amiez was third (1:36.19).
Austria's Thomas Sykora defied a hip injury sustained in a heavy fall before last Sunday's slalom in Kitzbuehel to improve on a first-leg ninth place for overall fourth (1:36.23).
Sykora has won five of the eight slaloms staged so far this season, finished second once and continues to head the slalom World Cup standings.
"I am happy Tomba won. Now he is the favorite for the Sestriere slalom," said Sykora. "This removes a lot of weight from my shoulders."
